transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. A Zanussi ZDT21006FA tripping its RCD about 15 minutes into a cycle strongly suggests an electrical fault that activates once the heating stage begins. The most common cause is the heater element developing a short to earth (ground) as it heats up or expands slightly. Less commonly, it could be the circulation pump or internal wiring. Please do not keep resetting the breaker and running the dishwasher, as this can worsen the fault or create a safety hazard. To help identify the specific component, does the trip happen precisely when you expect the water to start heating (usually 10–20 minutes in), or at a different time? Also, check if there is any burning smell or scorch marks on the plug or cable.

Yes it's usually 10-20 mins in, on the 65C programme. No burning smell, and I haven't looked at the plug closely but nothing seems damaged. It's on the same circuit as my fridge so I'd like to get it sorted.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The timing confirms it: tripping 10–20 minutes into a hot wash is classic for the heater element developing an earth fault as it heats up. Because this involves opening the appliance to access internal electrical components and testing live circuits, I cannot advise you on how to fix this yourself. You need a qualified appliance engineer to isolate the machine, test the heater element for continuity to earth, and replace it if faulty. Please do not attempt to reset the breaker again or run the dishwasher until it has been repaired.
